what_it_does: Graph neural networks (GNNs) process graphs—networks of connected entities—and dynamic GNNs repeat this computation across snapshots of a graph at different time steps, like analyzing a social network as it evolves minute by minute. Scaling this to multiple machines is hard because graph structure changes over time, creating complex data dependencies between snapshots and load imbalance across compute nodes. DiTile-DGNN solves this with redundancy-free parallelism: it analytically identifies which data is the same across snapshots and eliminates redundant computation. A separate optimizer removes synchronization barriers between snapshots, and the accelerator hardware reconfigures dynamically to support multiple computation patterns without redesign.
